articles.title: Venu, Vijay urge probe into SDTT’s action on Tata Sons
articles.description: Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh met with the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner to discuss concerns surrounding the legal actions of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust. They highlighted potential misuse of charitable resources in lawsuits involving Tata Sons and brought forth specific requests for transparency and an inquiry into the Trust's operations. Their primary objective is to safeguard public charitable funds from being utilized for regulatory disputes.

articles.title: IBM ends H-1B, green cards in consulting arm
articles.description: IBM has decided to stop work visa and green card sponsorship for most roles in its consulting division. Affected employees must choose to relocate outside the US or leave by December 31, 2026. The company will offer a severance package to those who do not relocate. This policy change is attributed to evolving business needs and a decrease in available skilled workers.

The proposed deal could give Tata Steel a 52.38% stake and control of APL Apollo.

articles.title: RBI brings more gold home, shifts 165 tonnes from overseas vaults
articles.description: Between September 2025 and September 2026, the Reserve Bank of India increased its domestic gold holdings significantly. The domestic share of gold rose from 65.4% to 84%, while holdings in international banks decreased. Total gold holdings changed minimally, increasing from 880.18 tonnes to 880.52 tonnes. The share of gold in foreign exchange reserves fluctuated during this period due to price changes.

articles.title: Harry Gestetner worked 100-hour weeks and slept just 5 hours a night before illness left him almost bedridden; in 2025, he founded sleep-tech startup Orion, that has generated $50 million and is targeting $100 million in 2027
articles.description: Orion smart mattress cover: Harry Gestetner spent his early years building Fanfix working 100-hour weeks and sleeping just five hours a night. After an inner-ear condition caused vertigo and left him struggling to get out of bed, he turned his attention to sleep and founded Orion in 2025. The sleep-tech startup has since generated more than $50 million in revenue.

articles.title: Private fuel retailers post sales decline in October
articles.description: Private fuel retailers, such as Reliance-BP and Nayara Energy, saw substantial declines in diesel and petrol sales. Higher fuel prices led customers to prefer state-run retail outlets like Indian Oil and Bharat Petroleum. As a result, state-run retailers increased their diesel and petrol sales significantly during October. The increase in demand from bulk customers also impacted the market dynamics in October.

articles.title: Tata Trusts vs Tata Sons: Chandrasekaran Reappointment Faces Court Challenge | News18
articles.description: A major boardroom battle within the Tata Group is moving towards the courtroom. The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust and the R.D. Tata Trust have passed resolutions authorising legal action in the Bombay High Court against the September 17 decision of the Tata Sons board to reappoint N. Chandrasekaran as executive chairman for another five-year term. The two trusts are challenging the validity of the board resolution, arguing that it did not secure the affirmative votes required under Article 121 of Tata Sons’ Articles of Association. The dispute centres on the voting process at the September 17 meeting, where Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata opposed Chandrasekaran’s reappointment, while director Venu Srinivasan supported it. articles.title: Retail borrowers’ corner over half of incremental NBFC credit as industrial lending slows
articles.description: NBFCs are shifting incremental lending towards retail borrowers, with retail loans accounting for nearly 57% of new credit in FY26 against 32% a year earlier, while industrys share fell to 26%, RBI data showed. The change has been driven by slower infrastructure lending and rapid growth in gold loans and other retail credit, even as unsecured lending and NBFCs dependence on bank funding continue to rise.

articles.title: India's top eight office markets may require 260 million sq ft of additional office space
articles.description: India's top eight office markets are projected to require an additional 260 million square feet of office space. This need arises from evolving workforce dynamics and increasing formal workforce participation in various sectors. Major cities like Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR lead in both talent and leasing activities. Tier II cities also show significant hiring growth and are enhancing their office infrastructure.

articles.title: India's top 8 cities need 260 million sq ft more office space to meet workforce density demands
articles.description: Cushman & Wakefield reports that India's top eight cities will need increased office space to accommodate employees. The current average office space per professional stands at approximately 80 sq ft. Achieving a benchmark of 100 sq ft necessitates an addition of 260 million sq ft. Bengaluru, Mumbai, and Delhi NCR lead in professional workforce numbers and job postings.
